title: Jeff Bezos’ Former Hedge Fund Is Buying Bitcoin Again
detail:
Jeff Bezos’ Former Hedge Fund Is Buying Bitcoin Again
Lockridge Okoth

BTC-USD
AMZN
BLK
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Jeff Bezos' Old Hedge Fund Is Back in Bitcoin D.E. Shaw. Photo by BeInCrypto

Before Jeff Bezos founded Amazon, he worked at a Wall Street hedge fund known for using computers to predict market moves. That same firm is now buying Bitcoin again, after previously selling its entire Bitcoin ETF portfolio.

New York-based D. E. Shaw purchased $89.9 million in BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF during the third quarter, according to its latest SEC filing.

The fund held no shares in the ETF three months earlier. Its return is striking because it previously held nearly half a billion dollars in Bitcoin ETFs before exiting those positions.

But its biggest moves were elsewhere.

Why Is D. E. Shaw Buying Bitcoin Stocks?

Founded in 1988 by former Columbia University professor David Shaw, the firm uses mathematical models to guide its investments.

Bezos joined in 1990 and became its youngest senior vice president before leaving to start Amazon. Today, the hedge fund manages more than $115 billion.

Its latest filing shows a much bigger appetite for companies that accumulate Bitcoin.

D. E. Shaw increased its holdings in Strategy (MSTR), formerly MicroStrategy, nearly fivefold. The position was valued at $131.6 million by September's end.

It also opened a new $23.6 million position in Strive (ASST), the Bitcoin-focused company co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy.

Both companies rank among the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holders.

Is Wall Street Betting on a Bitcoin Recovery?

D. E. Shaw's filing also reveals put options covering more Strategy shares than the fund owns outright. These contracts can gain value when the stock falls.

The firm simultaneously holds call options, which can benefit from rising prices, alongside substantial Strategy convertible bonds.

This suggests a more complicated trading strategy. The fund could be hedging its exposure or exploiting price differences between securities.

Its actual intentions remain unclear because regulatory filings exclude certain positions, including short sales and futures.

D. E. Shaw joins institutions such as Wells Fargo that expanded Bitcoin ETF exposure during the quarter.

The fund's next filing, due in February, will reveal whether these positions survived the latest market downturn.
